newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says banks to cut OTC dlr selling rate anew.
newsitem.headline: Manila says banks to cut OTC dlr selling rate anew.

text.p: Philippine central bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Thursday banks would further cut their over-the-counter (OTC) dollar selling rate.
The bankers agreed on Tuesday evening to cap their OTC dollar selling rate to four percent of the previous day's weighted average on the official market.
"They said they're going to reduce it some more," Singson told reporters.
The banks agreed to cap their selling rate due to a public outcry over the high selling rate immediately after the central bank announced a de facto peso devaluation on Friday.
Banks were selling dollars as high as 35 pesos to the dollar when the official market was trading at 29.00 to 30.00 pesos.
Individuals who need dollars of $5,000 or less primarily make up the OTC market.
